newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLO/Bund spread seen bit higher on auction.
newsitem.headline: OLO/Bund spread seen bit higher on auction.

text.p: Belgian linear bond futures stood three basis points higher in thin early trade on Wednesday, ahead of a four-day weekend.

The upcoming bond exchange auction on Tuesday will bring some new supply, but dealers said upward pressure on the OLO/Bund spread should be limited. "It will go out one or two centimes, not more," one Luxembourg-based dealer said.

On Tuesday, the Treasury is offering OLOs 27 (4.00 pct, Jan 2000), 6 (9.00 pct, March 2003), 19 (6.50 pct, March 2005) and 26 (6.25 pct, March 2007) against the OLOs 15 (6.75 pct, May 1997) and 8 (9.25 pct, Aug 1997).
For the 6.75 percent, May 25, 1997 OLO 15, it is the last time it comes up for exchange before final maturity.

There is still 98 billion francs outstanding in the issue. ABN-Amro Brussels said in a market commentary that because of the large size of the block outstanding, the ministry of finance might be a bit more aggressive to get the paper, which might weigh on OLOs.

Trade today is expected to remain thin as most players have already squared positions ahead of the market close on Thursday and Friday. -- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
